plainLanguage: The elbow bends and straightens much less in a cable cross-over than in a bench press.
qualifiers: The cable cross-over in this study is a related condition, not the index cable fly.
Elbow excursion in the cross-over rose significantly when load increased from 15 to 30 per cent of body weight, which the authors read as difficulty stabilising the elbow under heavier load.
The cable conditions showed markedly larger between-participant variation than the bench press conditions.

conditions: loads of 15 and 30 per cent of body weight, laboratory motion capture
scope.population: twenty healthy adults aged 18 to 45 with weight-training experience

sourceLinks.locator: Table 2 and Results 3.2 (elbow flexion-extension range of motion and moment; significance p < 0.0125)

statement: At matched external loads, elbow flexion-extension range of motion was far smaller in a standing cable cross-over than in a flat barbell bench press: 21.8 (SD 10.9) degrees against 79.5 (SD 6.2) degrees at 15 per cent of body weight.
